sections.h2: What is different about selling fast in Mount Vernon?
sections.html:
Mount Vernon adds a city transfer tax to the state one, so weigh every offer by what you keep after both. The city also leans hard on building records, and that shapes how smoothly a financed sale closes.

The Department of Buildings keeps permit records back to the late 1880s and notes that banks and title companies read them before closings. Open permits or a missing certificate of occupancy can slow a buyer who needs a mortgage, while a cash buyer can take that house in its current state.

Round up the deed, a payoff statement, recent tax bills and any rental or occupancy papers. Those cover most of what a buyer or title agent will ask in week one.

sections.h2: How does the Census describe Mount Vernon's housing?
sections.html:
Mount Vernon packs in people and renters. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 72,304 residents is 2.2 percent below the 2020 base of 73,907, spread across 4.39 square miles of land, and owners live in just 42.9 percent of homes.

Survey figures for 2020 to 2024 put a typical owner-occupied home at $484,000, rent at $1,629 and household income at $78,779. The average commute takes 35.0 minutes, a third of residents were born abroad, and 14.7 percent live below the poverty line. More detail is on the Census QuickFacts page for Mount Vernon.

Since more than half of homes are rented, many sellers here hold a two- or three-family building or inherited one. Those buildings bring occupancy inspections, tenant paperwork and sometimes a vacancy inspection. Cash buyers can often step into a tenanted building instead of waiting for it to empty.

sections.h2: What are Mount Vernon's neighborhoods and transit links?
sections.html:
Mount Vernon sits on the Bronx line, bounded by the Bronx River on the west and the Hutchinson River on the east, with Yonkers, Bronxville, New Rochelle and Pelham around it. Locals divide it into four sections.

  • Downtown, centered on Gramatan and Fourth Avenues, holds City Hall, the library and the Petrillo Plaza transit hub.
  • Mount Vernon Heights has hilly ground and the Sandford Boulevard shopping corridor.
  • The North Side is more residential, with Chester Heights, Fleetwood, Huntswood and Oakwood Heights, and many co-op buildings in Fleetwood.
  • The South Side includes Parkside and Vernon Park, with multifamily housing and industrial blocks near the Bronx.

Commuters value the trains: Metro-North's Harlem Line calls at Mount Vernon West and Fleetwood, and the New Haven Line at Mount Vernon East. Public schools fall under the Mount Vernon City School District, with eleven elementary, two middle, two high and one alternative high school. Families from Connecticut settled the area in 1664 as part of Eastchester, and the place became a village in 1853 and a city in 1892. St. Paul's Church is a National Historic Site on the South Side, and the Carnegie-funded public library opened downtown in 1904.

sections.h2: How large is the Mount Vernon city transfer tax?
sections.html:
Mount Vernon's tax equals 1.5 percent of whatever the price exceeds $50,000 by, and the grantor pays. Chapter 234 of the city code sets the payment window at 30 days from delivery of the deed, and it must be paid ahead of recording.

State tax at $2 per $500 comes on top. This table works the two out for three prices.

Sample seller transfer taxes in Mount Vernon (City Code Chapter 234, Article VII; NYS Department of Taxation and Finance)
Sale priceCity taxState taxCombined
$300,000$3,750$1,200$4,950
$484,000$6,510$1,936$8,446
$750,000$10,500$3,000$13,500

The $484,000 row mirrors the Census home value. Both parties swear to a joint return filed with the City Comptroller, whether or not tax is due. Paying late costs an 8 percent penalty plus 1.5 percent interest for each month, and the buyer picks up the bill if the seller is exempt. See that the amount shows on the closing statement.

sections.h2: What does the Mount Vernon Department of Buildings ask of sellers?
sections.html:
The Department of Buildings works from City Hall, 1 Roosevelt Square, Room 210. It issues permits, inspects work and handles certificates of occupancy, and its FAQ says a certificate is only required after major work or a change in use since the house was built.

To see what the city has on record, bring your block and lot number and read the file. If there is no certificate, you apply for one, and missing floor plans must be replaced by plans drawn to architectural standards. Permitted work that departs from the city's records has to be legalized with a new building permit.

  • A permit costs $80 plus $6 per $1,000 of estimated cost, and it stays valid for a year while insurance is current.
  • Roofs may hold two layers at most before all must come off.
  • Fences can reach four feet in front yards on mapped streets and six feet at the sides and rear.
  • Rental units face a vacancy inspection, and large multiple dwellings can face a building-wide task force inspection.

Work without a permit produces a violation and penalty fees. The owner carries the responsibility for permits even if a contractor files them.

sections.h2: When are Mount Vernon property taxes due, and how do grievances work?
sections.html:
City tax is billed in two installments, due January 31 and July 31, and county tax is due April 30. Payment options are the Finance Office counter, the mail, or Info-Tax Online, which charges 2.65 percent on cards and $1.50 per electronic check.

The Assessor builds the roll, logs each deed transfer and applies exemptions. A tentative roll appears by June 1, the Board of Assessment Review hears grievances on the third Tuesday in June from 4 to 8 pm, and the roll turns final August 1. The 2026 filing deadline was June 16 and has passed. Each parcel needs its own RP-524, and the law allows one grievance per property.

STAR runs differently here than many owners assume. Applicants since May 1, 2015 register with the state at tax.ny.gov/star and receive a credit check, not an exemption. Before selling, request a current payoff of any open city tax from the Finance Office. The city's payment page explains the options.

sections.h2: How is a Mount Vernon deed filed at the county level?
sections.html:
Recording happens at the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division, which also takes the state TP-584. For fee math the clerk sends filers to its online Property Records Electronic Portal, and taxes may be paid by ACH, certified check, bank check, attorney escrow check or an approved vendor's check.

The state's deadline falls on the 15th day after the deed is delivered. Since the city code wants proof of payment affixed to the deed before it is recorded, have your lawyer or title agent confirm that the Comptroller has been paid first.

faqs.q: Does Mount Vernon charge its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The city takes 1.5 percent of the price above $50,000, and the seller pays within 30 days of delivering the deed, before recording. New York's $2 per $500 is charged on top.

faqs.q: What would a $400,000 sale cost in transfer tax?
faqs.a: The city portion is $5,250, being 1.5 percent of $350,000, and the state portion is $1,600, so the seller owes $6,850.

faqs.q: Can I sell in Mount Vernon with no certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: A bank and title company will usually inspect the city's building file for a financed buyer. The Department of Buildings says a certificate is needed only after major work or a change of use. A cash buyer may take the property as-is.

faqs.q: What are the city and county tax due dates?
faqs.a: City tax is due January 31 and July 31. County tax is due April 30.

faqs.q: Where can I see my property's assessment?
faqs.a: The Assessor keeps the roll, and tentative and final versions are posted on the city website. The tentative roll is out by June 1 and becomes final on August 1.
